channel.title: Last Page
channel.description: Essays, blogs, reviews, notes and verse by O IV.

item.title: Just Another Day
item.description: Somewhere along the way, birthdays stopped feeling special.

item.title: Culture Was Never Meant to Stay Pure
item.description: On Halloween, cultural identity, and our rather selective understanding of tradition.

item.title: Well, Well, Well. America Has Made a Choice
item.description: The 2026 midterms, a Democratic comeback, and a reminder that even the most powerful presidents need voters.

item.title: Who Actually Discovered Gravity?
item.description: From Aristotle to Newton to Einstein, the story of how humanity slowly figured out why things fall.

item.title: Perhaps the INDIA Alliance Has Finally Found Its Voice
item.description: The November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan was more than a protest against electoral irregularities. It offered a glimpse of what a coordinated opposition could look like when its leaders finally stand together.

item.title: They Traded Ownership for Convenience
item.description: The internet didn’t just change how we consume media. Somewhere along the way, it convinced us to stop owning it.

item.title: Apple Is Selling Us Things We Don’t Need
item.description: From touchscreen MacBooks to glowing logos, the company that once told us not to chase gimmicks seems increasingly interested in selling them. Perhaps the problem is not what technology can do, but what capitalism wants us to buy.

item.title: The Midterms Have a New Battle: Claude vs ChatGPT
item.description: Behind America’s political campaigns, two AI philosophies are fighting for influence. One wants stronger safeguards, the other fears that regulation could slow the future. And ordinary people are caught between them.

item.title: When a Political Defeat Becomes an International Problem
item.description: Lula’s victory is about more than Brazil’s domestic politics. It challenges Trump’s influence in Latin America, raises questions about American intervention, and exposes how headlines can shape our understanding of political accountability.

item.title: Netanyahu May Have Lost the Election, But Has He Lost Power?
item.description: Israel’s election has left Netanyahu struggling to secure a parliamentary majority. But the growing influence of Arab parties and the possibility of an Eisenkot-led government have made the political outcome far more complicated.

item.title: The Midterms: Is Trump About to Lose His Grip on Washington?
item.description: Why America’s November elections matter, how Congress works, and why the results could become a serious problem for Donald Trump.

item.title: Lula's Victory Is Bigger Than Brazil
item.description: A victory for the Brazilian left, a setback for Trump's political ambitions, and a little more hope for the Amazon and the planet.

item.title: The Internet Is Showing Its Cracks, and Quantum Computing Is Waiting
item.description: A critical flaw in PHP has exposed how fragile our digital world can be. As AI accelerates cyberattacks and quantum computing threatens the foundations of encryption, the internet we know may be approaching its biggest transformation yet.

item.title: The Prison of Hope
item.description: The most dangerous prisons are not the ones that lock us in, but the ones that convince us our life begins somewhere else.

item.title: The Greatest Heist in History: How the weak seized the Thorne
item.description: Has Any Conqueror in History Done More Damage Than the One Who Never Raised a Weapon?

item.title: What Does It Mean to Be a Developing Nation When Our Children Are Hungry?
item.description: Three in every ten Indian children under five suffer from stunted growth. What does that say about the country we are building?

item.title: Own your time
item.description: I ask no one to be productive. A word they brought into existence because slavery sounded too much like subjugation. But apparently, being productive is now the measure of a growing life. Ambition is…

item.title: The First Stone
item.description: I no longer know what I believe about God, but the words of Jesus still make me stop and think.

item.title: A Democracy That Fears Protest Has Forgotten Its Purpose
item.description: From the Boat Club lawns to Jantar Mantar, the shrinking space for dissent raises a question I cannot ignore: if citizens cannot challenge those in power, what exactly are their democratic rights worth?

item.title: If Time Can Slow Down, What Exactly Is Time?
item.description: The more I learn about time, the less certain I become about what it actually is.

item.title: The World Is Burning Red And Are We Witnessing a Global Left Uprising?
item.description: From France to Albania, Argentina to India, the streets are filling with angry citizens, students and workers. The flags may differ, the demands may not be identical, but something is happening that deserves our attention.

item.title: The Boys Was Never About Superheroes
item.description: A brilliant satire of power, celebrity, and corruption that stumbled at the finish line but never lost sight of what made it special

item.title: Beautiful Ugly: A Brilliant Premise Buried Under a Terrible Ending
item.description: An atmospheric mystery that kept me turning pages, only to leave me wondering what the author was doing with her own story.

item.title: Pradhama Drishtya Kuttakkar: When Strategy Isn’t Enough
item.description: An engaging Malayalam crime thriller that tries to outsmart its audience but occasionally forgets to outsmart its own plot holes.

item.title: When Dissent Lands in Jail, Political Differences Must Take a Back Seat
item.description: The detention of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka raises questions about the right to protest, the limits of state power and the need for opposition unity.

item.title: Electoral Manipulation Is Not a Machine That Wins Every Election
item.description: Why BJP losing in Kerala or Tamil Nadu does not automatically disprove allegations of strategic electoral manipulation.

item.title: Backrooms: A Brilliant Mystery Without a Payoff
item.description: An unsettling concept, brilliant suspense, and a conclusion that left me wondering what the journey was all about.

item.title: Inquilab Zindabad: India’s Long History of Defiance
item.description: From the revolts against colonial rule to the Emergency and the protests of today, India’s history belongs to those who refused to be silenced.

item.title: When Democracy Begins to Look Like an Emergency
item.description: You do not need to declare an Emergency to make people feel that their democratic freedoms are under threat.

item.title: Lost: The Mystery Was Never Just the Island
item.description: From a plane crash and a fight for survival to one of television’s most ambitious explorations of fate, faith, and human nature.

item.description: The protests over the Election Commission are becoming a much larger question about trust in Indian democracy.
